aboutMore: ok the stuff that isn't about the machine: my dad drives me to the mall every saturday and reads a paperback in the food court for 3 hours while i play. he's finished 31 since march. we split an orange julius at 3. my nana joyce came to Tilt once and said i looked like i was 'drying a floor with my feet.' it's the best review i've ever gotten. i can clap any tempo from 90 to 200 exactly (nikki checked with a metronome, exactly). there's also a kid in a spider-man shirt who watches me from the claw machine every saturday and i'm teaching him next week. light mode first. i have a spare sweatband.

blog.title: saturdays with my dad (the food court)
blog.body: every saturday my dad drives me to the mall and drops me at Tilt at noon and goes to the food court and reads a paperback for 3 hours. he's finished 31 since march. last week i asked if he was bored. he said 'kev. i'm not reading. i'm watching you walk away from the car looking happy.' then he said 'the book's good too.' our deal: at 3 i find him at the table by the pretzel place and we split an orange julius (he gets the straw, i get the last third) and he asks 'how was it' and i say 'good' and he says 'good' and that's the whole conversation and it's the best conversation of my week. last saturday i was 2 greats off a personal best and he said 'i heard the machine from here.' it was loud. he nodded. it was the arcade nod. i think he learned it from doug.

blog.title: the kid in the spider-man shirt
blog.body: for 3 saturdays there's been a kid in a spider-man shirt standing by the claw machine just watching me. he's like 8. he never says anything. today he said 'can i try.' i said 'light mode first.' he did one song, Butterfly, lowest level, standing at the very edge of the pad, and he missed 90 percent of the arrows and fell off twice and he was smiling the whole time. doug came out from behind the counter, looked at the kid, looked at me, and nodded. a BIG one. i've never gotten a big one. i gave the kid my backup sweatband and he wore it as a BELT. i said 'it goes on your head.' he said 'it's a belt now.' i said ok. he's coming back next week with his mom. i'm bringing ankle support in his size. it cost me one song. i didn't miss it.

blog.title: attempt 31 (i tried to AAA it again)
blog.body: it's been 4 months since the AAA. i've tried to do it again 31 times. i keep a tally on the back of the songlist printout. best so far: 4 greats off. last saturday i got 2 greats and a clean finish and the machine said AA and i stood there with my hands on the bar and for the first time in 4 months i wasn't mad. i was just breathing. doug nodded from the back. i realized something: the first one happened when nobody was watching. it was just for me. maybe it didn't need to happen twice. maybe the first time was the whole thing. i'm still going to try on attempt 32. (the witness drive is still open. i still need a witness. i'm fine. i'm doing great.) ankle report: ok.

blog.title: nana joyce reviews my set
blog.body: my nana joyce came to Tilt for the first time. she's 81. she sat on a stool next to the prize counter with her purse on her lap like she was at the bank. i did Butterfly on heavy. at the end she clapped once. she said 'you look like you're drying a floor with your feet.' dad laughed so hard he had to leave. i said 'is that good.' she said 'it's very thorough.' i've decided it's the best review i've ever gotten. then she handed me a $5 bill folded in a tiny square and said 'for quarters. don't tell your mother.' her daughter is my mother. i told my mother. my mother said 'she does that.' i have 20 quarters. nana stayed for the next song too. she hummed it. she didn't know what it was. it was Butterfly. she hummed it perfectly.

survey.title: THE WARMUP SURVEY (stretch first, then answer)
qa: name:
kevin. ddr_kevin online. 'kev' to my dad. 'the kid with the pillow' to my downstairs neighbor
who drives you to the mall:
my dad. every saturday. he reads a paperback in the food court for 3 hours. 31 books since march. i never asked him to
favorite snack:
orange julius, last third. my dad gets the straw. that's the deal. it's the best deal i've made
something you've never told anyone:
i say 'good game' to the machine when i leave. out loud. quietly. nobody has ever heard me. doug maybe heard me. he nodded at nothing once
what do you do besides ddr:
i can clap any tempo from 90 to 200 exactly. nikki checked it with a metronome. it's useless. it's mine
last time you were scared:
when the kid in the spider-man shirt said 'can i try' and i realized i'd have to be a person he looked up to. it was scarier than heavy mode
how's the ankle:
ok. dr feldman said 'rest.' i said 'what about on days that end in y.' he said 'reduce.' i said ok. i'm reducing. 31 to 29
best nod you've ever gotten:
doug's BIG one, when the kid fell off the pad twice and kept smiling. it was longer than a normal nod. it had a second half
something you're bad at:
being a witness. i've been looking for one for 4 months. you'd think the world would have more witnesses. it doesn't
pets:
a pillow with tape arrows on it. technically a pet. it has never once complained
what's in your gym bag:
a spare sweatband, ankle support (2), a songlist printout with tally marks, 20 quarters from nana, a banana (banana's idea)
favorite song that isn't ddr:
the sound of the machine warming up at noon. the little chirp. it's the best song i know
describe yourself in one sentence:
i'm a kid who does one thing very hard in a mall on saturdays, and my dad reads a book 40 feet away and is proud of me, and that's the whole story and it's enough

dms: a mall security guard (not dennis, the other one, his name tag says pat) stopped me on the escalator and said 'son, please don't dance on the escalator.' i said 'it's rhythm.' he said 'i know. i played trombone.' we did the whole ride on beat. at the top he took his hat off. i've never felt so understood by an authority figure

the podiatrist (dr feldman) said 'rest.' i said 'what about on days that end in y.' he looked at me for a long time. he wrote 'insoles' and 'reduce.' i asked what 'reduce' means. he said 'fewer than you're thinking.' i got insoles. they're the same color as my sweatband. coincidence. (i asked.)

{you} does a pretzel count as stretching. asking for my dad. he says it's 'carb loading.' i said that's for marathons. he said 'it's a very long book.' we split one. it was a good pretzel. the book was not mentioned

i can clap any tempo from 90 to 200 exactly. nikki checked. bryan asked me to clap 168 and i did and his metronome said 168.0. he said 'dude. you're a drum machine.' i said i'm a dancer. he said 'same.' we shook hands. it's the weirdest thing i can do and i love it

{you} i read malten's 'Why do I create?' and i think someone created the first step pattern. like somebody sat down and thought 'what if arrows. but on the floor.' i'd like to shake their hand and check their ankles. is that a creating answer. 'because someone has to put the arrows on the floor.' i'm gonna stretch on that

usagi taught me a word. 'tadaima.' it means 'i'm home.' i said it when i walked into Tilt and doug said 'what.' i said 'i'm home.' he said 'okay,' which isn't the word but it's close enough that i accepted it. doug's on a streak

i took the school stairs on beat today and the vice principal said 'kevin. walk.' i said 'i AM walking.' he said 'on beat.' i said yes. he said 'fine.' then he did the last 3 steps on beat. i'm not saying he's a convert. i'm saying he's a witness. the search is OPEN

dmitri (the counter-strike kid in duluth) and i compared notes on aim. he's rushed B about 4,000 times with a 61% win rate. i did the math. i've done Butterfly maybe 400 times with one AAA. different games, same hours. he said 'respect.' i said 'rush B.' he said 'what.' i said 'i don't know, it felt right.' he said 'it always does.'

a pigeon in the mall food court has been bobbing on beat to Butterfly for 3 saturdays. i've named him Doug Jr. he doesn't know. nobody knows. i'm telling you because you're the only one who can keep it secret
repliesExtra: perfect. no greats. all perfects. i'm saying that about ur message. it's the highest honor i have
that's an arcade nod. a real one. it means i heard u, i respect u and i'll remember it
hold on i'm stretching. i stretch before i read anything important. ok. ok good. ok that was great
my dad would say 'good' and that would be the whole conversation and it would be the best one of my week. so: good
light mode first. that's my advice for any new thing. light, then standard. never start on heavy. except Butterfly. that was an exception. don't tell anyone
i can tell from how u type that ur at about 120 bpm. it's steady. it's a good tempo. keep it
my nana joyce would say 'it's very thorough.' that's the highest compliment. so: very thorough
combo continues. i'm not letting ur message break it. it's the most important combo i have
doug nodded at this (in my head). it was a big one. it had a second half
thanks. that made my ankles feel better. which is a lot. (they're sore.) (they're fine.)
statusesExtra: kevin stretched for 20 minutes at the mall and a lady asked if he was 'warming up for something.' kevin said 'life.' she said 'oh good.' he's never been so understood by a stranger

kevin is on attempt 31 of the repeat AAA. 2 greats. he wasn't mad. doug nodded from the back. new personal best in not being mad.
kevin found out nana joyce has been practicing 'drying a floor with her feet' in the kitchen. his mom filmed it. he has not seen it. he's afraid. he's also proud
kevin can now clap 172 exactly, 168 exactly, and 'about 140 but with feeling.' nikki says the last one doesn't count. it counts

kevin i checked ur clapping against a metronome. 172.0. it's perfect. the metronome was worried. ur the most accurate person i know. also i'm making a 90 to 200 test mix. u can't cheat. UNTZ

KEVIN. rhythm brother. i got 5 stars on Free Bird on expert and then i tried ur Butterfly on the pad and got a D. u're a different kind of expert. i respect it. an AAA with no witnesses is real. same as a sold out show where my sister counted the tickets. also do u want to be my drummer. i don't have a band but i'm assembling one

Dear Kevin, I am told you can dance on a mat to a machine. I danced at one wedding in my life, once, and only after I was told. Dorothy led. I have always thought a person who moves in time is a person who listens. Regards, Walt

KEVIN. my host brother sven saw the machine at the mall and said 'that is eurodance but on the floor.' he got a D. he's going back saturday. u have a new student. also grandpa gene says u should SCORE every song like baseball. '8 greats, 2 misses.' it's all there. GO

gus: gus i saw ur 5 stars on expert. that's real. that's the same kind of exact as a perfect on heavy. we both press a thing at the right time. come to tilt saturday. i'll hold the guitar, u hold the pad. we swap. it's called a dangerous exchange. nobody has done it

gus u asked if i think ur 'a real guitarist.' honest answer: a real guitarist plays a real guitar. a real expert presses the right thing at the right time. both are real. one has strings. i respect the strings. i also respect the green button. come play the pad. the pad is real
ben: ben u got an E on butterfly on heavy. that's ok. i got an E my first 40 times. u're 40 minus 1 away from a D. squad 7 needs a taijutsu guy?? i'm flattered. i don't know what that is but i know feet. put me on the list (i don't know what the list is)

ben i watched ur arms back run. it's actually a decent heavy mode stance. wide base. but keep ur arms forward. the wind isn't the problem. it's the arms. i believe in u. BELIEVE IT. (doug nodded when i said that.)
penny: penny the glow tape is IN. i put it on the pillow at home (green left, pink right, blue for the ones i don't know yet). the pillow glows now. my downstairs neighbor did 'broom on ceiling' and then asked what the light was. a duet AND a rave. thank u

penny the sweatbracelet fits under the sweatband. i wear both. doug said 'what's that' and i said 'penny' and he nodded. a nod for u. u're on the nod list. it's a short list. 3 names. doug, my dad, u. (the slushie order is load-bearing. usagi taught me that.)
dmitri: dmitri u told me u've rushed B about 4,000 times with a 61% win rate. that's a practice log. i have a practice log too. mine's tally marks on the back of a songlist. we do the one thing 4,000 times and call it strategy. come to tilt if u ever get to ohio. there's a pad with ur name on it (it says kevin) (it's mine) (i'll share)

dmitri u told me the best part of a lan party is 'the guy who shows up with the extension cord.' i'm the guy with the sweatband. we're the same. we both bring the thing the room needs. also u said 'mom says dinner' is a legal callout. my dad says 'good' is a legal callout. we're in the same league
